description: BatteryML is Microsoft's Python toolkit for preparing battery test data and benchmarking machine-learning models of degradation. It provides data-source adapters, feature engineering and configurable training/inference workflows for remaining-useful-life prediction. The README lists several public cell datasets and supports ARBIN and NEWARE cycler exports through editable field mappings. Outputs are standardised BatteryData objects, learned models and benchmark results. Coverage is global at cell-test level, with chemistry, cycle histories and sample counts determined by each source, not a uniform observation period. Public code and command-line setup are free under MIT, while source datasets retain their own conditions. A limitation is that cycler formats vary across software versions and default mappings may require changes. Additional cycler formats are described as being integrated, so their availability is not assumed. The toolkit can support calibration of storage-degradation assumptions in infrastructure simulations, complementary to system-level PyPSA modelling (model-pypsa). The ICLR 2024 article describes the resource; reported benchmark scores were not independently reproduced. No raw battery data were downloaded.
name: BatteryML
